options.command: echo 'copying dbx-analytics license' && cp LICENSE dist/packages/dbx-analytics

metadata.description: The flat case -- dbx-analytics has no secondary entry points, so this target is just the post-step wrapper around build-base. What changed: the nested `npx nx run dbx-analytics:build-base:production` shell-out became a dependsOn EDGE, so the build is one Nx process and one task graph instead of a parent process shelling out to a child one. The `:production` suffix is not lost by dropping it: a TargetDependencyConfig has no `configuration` field, but Nx's resolveConfiguration falls back to the target's `defaultConfiguration`, and build-base declares `production` as exactly that.  This also fixes a live bug. `parallel` was unset on the old two-command build, which defaults to TRUE, so `cp LICENSE` raced ng-packagr -- and lost: dist/packages/dbx-analytics shipped with no LICENSE file at all, because @nx/angular:package deletes its whole dest directory before writing. With the copy as this target's OWN command it cannot start until build-base has finished.

`^build`, not `^build-base`. @nx/js remaps @dereekb/* imports to the dist DIRECTORY, so TypeScript reads that directory's package.json `exports` to resolve them -- and the dependency's own `build` is what finalizes those exports. Declared explicitly rather than inherited from the `@nx/angular:package` targetDefault in nx.json so the edge is visible where it matters; the value is the same.
